Resolves #21201

The engine now ships a whole web desktop. `Neo.desktop.Container` is one component a consumer drops in: the workspace with the launcher, the taskbar with its start menu and the open apps, and the app windows, which it opens through the `Neo.desktop.WindowManager` it owns. `examples/desktop/basic` is its second consumer, with no controller. The web desktop demo is its first, and keeps only its sign-in, permissions and data. #21272's window-controls contract is AC-5 to AC-7 here.

Third leaf of #21198, re-cut onto `dev` after #21305 and #21310 landed. Engine 14 line: Thu 19 Nov, 24:00 UTC (#21198's Timing).

**What moved, and what is new.** Moved from the demo with behavior unchanged: `Desktop.mjs` (now `Neo.desktop.Container`), `Taskbar.mjs`, `TaskList.mjs` and `AppWindow.mjs`, plus the controller's window wiring, start menu and task clicks, and their four stylesheets (now `resources/css/src/desktop/`, with values per theme). The new seams, where the review should look:
- `Neo.desktop.AppWindow#record` is the window's only input: the title and the header icon follow it, and its items read it as `data.record`. The container makes itself each window's `parentComponent`, so the window's provider continues into the consumer's.
- The container's `items` map, `launcherConfig` and `taskbarConfig`: a consumer adds a side panel or taskbar items by key and `weight`. The demo adds its permission panel and four taskbar items.
- #21272's window controls. `dialog.Base` dresses maximize as a `Neo.toolbar.ActionButton` toggle (the dock's primitive), so `maximized` sets its glyph and its name ("maximize" or "restore"). `toolbar.Base#actionMap` merges per entry, and the window manager contributes minimize to the windows it can restore.

Evidence: L2 (unit on every new class, real-Chromium e2e on the example and the demo) → L2 required.

| AC-3 | `resources/css/src/desktop/{Container,AppWindow,Taskbar,TaskList}.css`, with neo-dark and neo-light values in `theme-neo-*/desktop/` and the phone layout included. The demo's four shell sheets are gone, and so are its menu and wallpaper values. |
| AC-4 | CI-covered: `PhoneAndTouch.spec.mjs` 2/2 and the demo's unit specs. The viewport holds the sign-in and the container, with its panel and note by key and its taskbar items in `WebDesktop.view.Taskbar`. Frames below: the demo is unchanged but for the app icon now in the window header. |
| AC-5 | CI-covered: `dialog/WindowControls.spec.mjs` (glyph and name both ways, programmatic and at construction); `Basic.spec.mjs` checks the restore glyph against minimize's. |

## Deltas from ticket
- **Styles are CSS**, not SCSS: #21225 moved the theme sources.
- **Minimize is the manager's contribution**, not an `AppWindow` action, so it appears only on windows a manager can restore, whatever their class.
- **The demo keeps a taskbar subclass** for its four items, so their accessible-name arm still has a unit to create.
- **The start menu's handler** is `up.onStartMenuAppChoose` on the generic `model.App`, so a chosen app reaches the container with no consumer code. The container opens the store's record, not the menu's copy.
- **#21272 is marked completed by hand** after merge: a pull request resolves one ticket.

## Cold look
Two readers without session context graded the unlabelled frames from 1 to 10 for "a finished, believable product a visitor would trust", with the demo pair in swapped order:

| Frame | Reader A | Reader B |
|---|---|---|
| demo, base | 6 | 5 |
| demo, head | 6.5 | 6 |
| example | 5 | 4 |

Both readers prefer the head and name the same difference: the app icon in the window header. Both also name the same gap. Every window body is a placeholder (an icon, a tagline, a permission chip in the demo; one sentence in the example), and the minimize, maximize and close glyphs look mismatched beside the app icons. Neither gap is this leaf's: it moves the shell, and AC-4 keeps the demo unchanged. Real apps in the windows and the window chrome are the design follow-up, to be coordinated with #21331.

## Post-Merge Validation
- [ ] #21139: the demo's open checks run again.
- [ ] #21272: marked completed by hand, linking this pull request.

Intake: self-authored; the drift probe fired (CSS since #21225; `dialog/Base.mjs` at #21283 moved only move and resize). Core idioms read: `src/core/Base.mjs` (instance merge applies to reactive configs only, hence `actionMap_`), `src/Neo.mjs` (descriptor merges), `src/state/Provider.mjs` (a provider's parent through `component.parent`, so `parentComponent`). Siblings: `app.content.Container` (`items` map, `[mergeFrom]` part configs) and the dock's maximize (`ActionButton` toggle).

The app-store swap can likewise retain a cached window bound to the previous record for the same ID. Support live replacement coherently or reject unsupported replacements before changing any consumer or destroying an owned store. Cover an open or minimized window and preserve unrelated records in a supplied shared store.
      **Commit:** `a102d57025`
      **Details:** Supported live, in `Neo.desktop.WindowManager`, so every consumer gets it and not only the container.
      - `taskStore_` is reactive now. A replacing task store takes over the manager's tasks: each leaves the old store (if it still exists; the container may have destroyed a store it created), comes back in the new one rebuilt from its app and its window, and is minimized if the window is hidden. A key another owner holds in the new store leaves the window without a task of this manager. The old store keeps only other owners' records.
      - A replacing app store first runs the filter pass, as #21305 pinned (the catalog-swap arm). The windows and tasks of the apps it keeps then bind to its records: `AppWindow#record`, and the task's text, icon and colour.
      - New arms: a minimized window across a task-store swap, with an unrelated record kept, restore, and a destroy that leaves no task; and kept windows rebound across an app-store swap (`WindowManagerDialog.spec.mjs`, `WindowManager.spec.mjs`).

In the already-supported shared-store collision, the second manager's same-ID window opens without its own task. `WindowManager.#offerMinimize` still contributes a visible control, while `minimize` and `restore` require that manager's task. Pin the first manager's working minimize/restore and the second window's unavailable control without touching the first task.
      **Commit:** `a102d57025`
      **Details:** Minimize is still offered at creation, so the first render holds it. Every open runs `#syncMinimize`, which takes the offer back when the manager holds no task of its own and offers it again when it does. The new arm pins the first manager's minimize and restore, the second window's absent control, and the first task surviving the second manager's destroy.

- [x] **`[ADDRESSED]`** Keep the maximize/restore glyph and accessible name synchronous across action rebuilds (AC-5). With a maximized dialog, changing `headerToolbar.actions` to `['close', 'maximize']` constructs an unpressed "maximize" control. Materialize or resynchronize it from the current dialog state and pin this reconfiguration alongside the existing construction and toggle arms.
      **Commit:** `a102d57025`
      **Details:** The dialog listens to its header's `actionsChange` and resyncs maximize, so a rebuilt control states `maximized` again. Building it pressed did not work: an `ActionButton` created with `pressed: true` does not apply its pressed glyph and name. The new arm in `dialog/WindowControls.spec.mjs` sits beside the construction and toggle arms.
